meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, go out

meanings.en: to meet; to date, go out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet; to date, go out', paired with 'встретиться'.

examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already.

examples.text: Мы уже месяц встречаемся. Мне надоело уже.
examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already. I'm tired of it already.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щительный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sociable, outgoing').

examples.text: Он такой милый и очень общительный!
examples.trans: He is so sweet and very sociable!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

examples.text: Красивая. Но это же не ваша жена! Я вашу жену видел.
examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'юрприз'). Common masculine noun meaning 'surprise' in everyday Russian.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'holiday voucher, package trip' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a holiday voucher for the seaside.

examples.text: Путёвки на двоих, в Крым. Март, начало сезона.
examples.trans: Holiday vouchers for two, to Crimea. March, the start of the season.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лететь'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fly, to start flying'.

examples.text: Я из-за тебя не полетела в Милан!
examples.trans: I missed the Milan trip because of you!
Tomorrow we will fly to rest, okay?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'genius' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This artist is a true genius.
He has the talent of a genius.

examples.text: Вы гений и выдающийся ум современности!
examples.trans: You are a genius and the greatest mind of our time!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'бросить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw out, discard', paired with 'выбрасывать'.

examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window.

examples.text: Он мэра в окно выбросил. Вы помните?
examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window. Do you remember?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мойка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'dumpster, trash heap, rubbish dump' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take the bag to the trash dump.

examples.text: Ладно, я отнесу её на помойку.
examples.trans: Okay, I will take it to the dumpster.
He found a box in the dumpster.
